items.title: Your Talent Insights from Ashby This Month
items.sponsor_flag: Yes - the headline report ('Recruiter Productivity 2026') is Ashby's own product/dataset, and the newsletter is Ashby's own community newsletter promoting its product updates. Treat the applications-per-hire and offer-conversion figures as Ashby's own data, not independent research.

points.claim: Applications per hire have nearly tripled since 2021, and interview rates have roughly halved, which recruiters can cite when justifying screening headcount or AI-assisted triage to stakeholders.
points.evidence: Applications per hire rose from 100 (2021) to 291 (2026); interview rate fell ~50%
points.quote: applications per hire increased from 100 in 2021 to an average of 291 today, the share of candidates receiving an interview fell by about 50%
points.paywall: no - full report free to read on Ashby's site (per newsletter); not independently verified here

points.claim: Offer conversion rates recruiters could benchmark against: business roles convert nearly 50% better than technical roles.
points.evidence: Q1 2026 offer conversion: 10.4% business roles, 7.3% technical roles
points.quote: offer conversion reached 10.4% for business roles and 7.3% for technical roles

points.claim: AI use is already bleeding across job functions at HR-specific rates recruiters could quote when discussing AI adoption internally.
points.evidence: OpenAI report: 43.5% of occupation-specific ChatGPT use crosses into other jobs' tasks, rising to 69% for HR
points.quote: 43.5% of occupation-specific ChatGPT use crosses into tasks associated with other jobs, rising to 69% for HR
points.paywall: not stated (OpenAI report link not given in file)

points.claim: A recruiting leader argues take-home assessments should now test how candidates use AI, not whether they can avoid it - a reframe TA could apply to their own assessment design this week.
points.evidence: Chris Abbass, CEO of Talentful
points.quote: assessments should focus on how candidates use AI - framing problems, challenging outputs, catching mistakes, explaining decisions

items.title: The Future of Recruiting: Talent Advisor vs. Talent Engineer
items.sponsor_flag: No sponsor slot noted; figures are cited from third-party academic/field studies (Microsoft, MIT researchers, BCG), not the newsletter's own product.

points.claim: AI tools cut individual admin work (email) but do not yet reduce meeting time, useful for setting realistic expectations with stakeholders about where AI actually saves hours.
points.evidence: Microsoft study of 6,000 knowledge workers, 6-month randomized field experiment
points.quote: spent 3 fewer hours on email each week, while meeting time did not change in a meaningful way

points.claim: AI tools disproportionately help less-skilled workers, a number recruiters could use to justify rolling out AI tools team-wide rather than only to senior staff.
points.evidence: Study of 5,179 customer support agents (Brynjolfsson, Li, Raymond)
points.quote: Productivity rose 14% on average, while productivity among novice and lower-skilled workers improved by 34%

points.claim: AI speeds up in-scope tasks dramatically but actively hurts accuracy on out-of-scope tasks - a caution for recruiters trusting AI outputs blindly.
points.evidence: Field experiment, 758 Boston Consulting Group consultants, 18 tasks
points.quote: completed 12.2% more tasks and worked 25.1% faster, with quality scores more than 40% higher

points.claim: Confidence in AI without confidence in yourself dulls critical thinking - a one-line prompt for recruiters to self-check before accepting an AI recommendation on a candidate.
points.evidence: Microsoft/Carnegie Mellon survey of 319 knowledge workers, 936 examples of GenAI use
points.quote: Higher confidence in AI was associated with less critical thinking

items.title: Who Gets to Win the AI Talent Boom?
items.sponsor_flag: No sponsor slot flagged in the file. The 'Build of the Week' profiles a named individual's independent project (not the newsletter's own product); figures in the Big Idea section attributed to LinkedIn research, treat as third-party.

points.claim: A recruiter with no engineering background built a working recruiting intelligence platform using off-the-shelf AI tools, a concrete template TA readers could follow one step further than a simple automation.
points.evidence: Michael Brinn built Insyt using Claude (spec), Lovable (prototype), Supabase (database), then Claude Code for the real build
points.quote: used Claude to define Insyt's three user views, scoring model, and permissions before building a single screen

points.claim: New H-1B extension fees landing in September will raise the cost of sponsoring US visa holders, relevant for any TA team hiring internationally into the US.
points.evidence: $4,000 additional fee on certain H-1B extensions from September 9; $4,500 extra on some L-1 extensions
points.quote: Employers filing certain H-1B extensions face an additional $4,000 fee starting September 9

points.claim: AI leadership roles remain heavily male-skewed globally, a stat TA leaders working on DEI in AI hiring could quote.
points.evidence: LinkedIn research: women 26% of US AI hires in 2025; 13% of C-suite AI leadership roles across 27 countries
points.quote: Women accounted for just 26% of US AI hires in 2025, and hold only 13% of C-suite AI leadership roles at AI companies across 27 countries

points.claim: AI job postings and pay have surged, giving TA a current benchmark figure for AI-role salary conversations.
points.evidence: AI job postings roughly doubled since 2023; typical advertised salary ~$177,000
points.quote: AI job postings in the US have roughly doubled since 2023, typical advertised salary around $177,000

items.title: Week of August 10th, 2026
items.sponsor_flag: Newsletter states it is sponsor-free ('We are sponsor-free. No company below has paid us to advertise their products'); vendor product updates are unpaid community-submitted mentions, not sponsor slots or the newsletter's own product.
items.gap_note: This issue is a link/roundup digest (community advice column plus a curated list of articles, vendor updates, events and job postings) with almost no standalone figures or verbatim data points to extract - most items are just names/titles pointing to other people's content, not quotable claims in themselves.

points.claim: A RecOps community voice argues leaders should deliberately pull ops-track hires out of candidate-experience work to force new skill growth, a tactic a TA leader restructuring a coordinator's role could apply this week.
points.evidence: Advice column by Jeremy Lyons, RecOps Collective
points.quote: I would try to steer completely out of candidate experience

points.claim: Metaview acquired Reval to accelerate its Fillmore product, a named M&A move relevant to TA teams evaluating agentic hiring platforms.
points.evidence: Metaview (Agentic AI Hiring Platform) acquisition of Reval
points.quote: Acquired Reval to accelerate Fillmore

points.claim: GoodTime's new scheduling agent 'Cori' takes voice or text scheduling instructions and acts with approval, a concrete off-the-shelf tool a TA reader could trial for interview scheduling.
points.evidence: GoodTime (Scheduling) product release: Cori
points.quote: give scheduling instructions by voice or text, let Cori gather the missing details, confirm the plan, and take action with your approval

points.claim: Ashby added the ability to view and save candidate email attachments directly from the candidate profile, a small but usable workflow tweak for teams already on Ashby.
points.evidence: Ashby (AiO) product release
points.quote: View and save candidate email attachments from the candidate profile

items.title: Hiring is a team sport. Your ATS should be too.
items.sponsor_flag: Yes - the 92% figure is an explicit sponsor mention for Metaview's Application Review agent, not independent research or the newsletter's own data.

points.claim: A sponsor-claimed AI screening agent reportedly cuts inbound-screening time dramatically, a number to treat with caution as a vendor claim when pitching similar tools internally.
points.evidence: Metaview's Application Review agent - sponsor claim
points.quote: Teams using it are seeing up to 92% less time spent on inbound screening

points.claim: The article argues ATS systems only formally recognise Recruiter and Hiring Manager roles, missing referrers and panel members who also handle candidate data - useful framing for a TA reader auditing who touches candidate data outside the ATS.
points.evidence: Core argument of the piece
points.quote: None of these people is recruiters. None of them appears in the process map. But all of them are recruiting.

points.claim: When the ATS doesn't support a workflow, candidate data leaks into ungoverned email threads - a prompt for TA to check where CVs go once the ATS says no.
points.evidence: Core argument of the piece
points.quote: when the system says no, email says yes

points.claim: A practical five-question checklist a TA reader could literally run against their own ATS setup this week.
points.evidence: Practical checklist offered in the piece
points.quote: Does every requisition have a defined hiring team?
